counterfactual_missing_items: No sinus node dysfunction (sinus arrest, sinoatrial block, or tachy-brady pattern) to support sick sinus syndrome.
No severe aortic stenosis or valve-related syncope; AS is only moderate and echo shows preserved function.
No alternative reversible cause of AV block (e.g., ischemia, hyperkalemia, drug effect) is documented.
decisive_items: Prolongation of the His-His interval from the second to third beats results in phase IV block within the His-Purkinje system.
Block initiates after a premature atrial complex and transiently resolves following another premature atrial complex
Shows 6 P waves conducting to the ventricle, followed by a period of atrioventricular block
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete and precise: the intracardiac recording explicitly localizes the AV block to the His-Purkinje system as phase IV block, and the ECG shows PAC-triggered AV block. R2 captures AV block but omits the His-Purkinje localization and is discounted as a correlated less-specific restatement; R3 misreads telemetry pauses as sinus node dysfunction despite AV block; R4 is an incidental moderate AS finding that does not explain the conduction block.

rejected.why: Correlated less-specific restatement of C1; lacks His-Purkinje localization.
Pauses are due to AV block, not sinus node dysfunction; no sinus node abnormality on ECG.
Moderate AS is a comorbidity; does not explain telemetry pauses or His-Purkinje block.
